1_incident_name: Oakridge Industrial Park Anhydrous Ammonia Release

4_map_sketch.total_area_of_operations: 2.0-mile radius centered at Cold Storage Logistics Building 7, Edison, NJ.
4_map_sketch.incident_site_area: Mechanical Room 3 on roof deck of Cold Storage Logistics Building 7 (100 Industrial Parkway), where an 8-inch high-pressure ammonia chiller line fractured.
4_map_sketch.impacted_areas: 400-yard vapor dispersion plume encompassing Building 7 loading dock and northern section of Industrial Parkway.
4_map_sketch.threatened_areas: Meadowlands Residential Community (0.9 miles East downwind) and Edison Transit Center (1.2 miles Southeast).
4_map_sketch.overflight_results: Edison Police Drone Recon Unit DRONE-PD-1 confirmed a dense white fog cloud hovering over Roof Mechanical Room 3 and drifting East-Northeast at 5 mph.
4_map_sketch.trajectories: Airborne toxic anhydrous ammonia cloud migrating East-Northeast at 5 mph; zero liquid chemical product entering storm drainage systems.
4_map_sketch.impacted_shorelines: None; contamination restricted to localized industrial ground surfaces and rooftop structures.
4_map_sketch.graphics_and_symbology: North oriented vertically, depicting Staging Area Foxtrot at Edison High School parking lot, Command Post at Edison Fire Station 4, 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone boundary, and Industrial Parkway traffic control points.

5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.situation_summary: At 07:45 EDT on 09/05/2026, a mechanical vibration failure severed an 8-inch liquid refrigeration line inside Mechanical Room 3 at Cold Storage Logistics, releasing approximately 3,000 lbs of anhydrous ammonia gas. Building 7 was evacuated immediately (85 employees), and a 1,000-foot perimeter isolation zone was established.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.health_and_safety_hazards: Severe chemical asphyxiation, acute pulmonary edema, permanent ocular injury, cryogenic chemical freeze burns, flammability risk in enclosed spaces (LEL 15-28%), and physical fall hazards from roof decking.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.necessary_measures: Mandatory 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone; Level A encapsulated vapor suits with SCBA for all roof entry personnel; Level B suits for ground backup teams; continuous electrochemical ammonia air monitoring at perimeter boundaries; high-volume water curtain deployment for vapor knockdown; mandatory dual-basin chemical wash decontamination corridor at Building 7 main entrance.

7_current_and_planned_objectives: Enforce 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone and isolate Building 7 HVAC intake by 08:30 hours.
Perform roof entry under Level A PPE to manually isolate main receiver valve by 11:00 hours.
Deploy high-volume water curtain monitoring nozzles to suppress cloud drift by 09:30 hours.
Perform continuous downwind air monitoring along Meadowlands border by 09:00 hours.
Establish Unified Command (Edison Fire, NJ DEP, EPA R2, Facility RP) by 08:45 hours.

8_current_and_planned_actions_strategies.actions: Initial alarm dispatch; Edison Fire Engines 4 and 6 respond and assist Building 7 evacuation.
Local Command established by Chief E. Sullivan; Industrial Parkway closed at Kilmer Road.
Middlesex County Hazmat Team 2 arrived to set up perimeter air monitoring grid and water fog curtain monitors.
NJ DEP and EPA Region 2 OSC arrived on scene; Unified Command established at Station 4.
Drone recon flight confirmed water curtains reduced downwind cloud density by 60%.
Planned: Entry Team 1 under Level A PPE executes emergency roof entry to isolate main refrigeration manifold.
Planned: Initiate mechanical ventilation of Building 7 interior through charcoal scrubber array.
Planned: Conduct clearance air sampling inside Building 7 prior to facility re-entry.

10_resource_summary.notes: Operating water curtains and preparing Level A roof entry.
Supplying high-pressure water to fog monitors for vapor suppression.
Positioned for roof access and aerial water stream deployment.
Conducting continuous thermal and aerial monitoring of plume drift.
En route to perform positive pressure building scrubbing.
En route to monitor downwind Meadowlands residential perimeter.
